title: Who may sign in, and an administrator's admission changes
description: GET /api/v1/server/access lists every admission source: operator (root's site.json, never removable here), site_admin (runtime entries the broker keeps) and team (people a listed GitHub team admitted at a sign-in), with the listed teams. POST /api/v1/server/access/teams/add {team} lists organisation/team (a slug, or the team's github.com/orgs/…/teams/… address) as a source: its organisation is resolved through GitHub's public API (github_org_not_found), a malformed name is invalid_team, and the reply is the teams. POST /api/v1/server/access/teams/remove {org_id, slug} removes one; what it gave ends at each member's next sign-in. POST /api/v1/server/access/forget {id} dismisses a leaver's notice: a team row that no longer admits goes, and rejoining admits again at a sign-in. A row whose account was created at a sign-in under a site onboarding configuration carries onboarding, that sign-in's receipt. POST /api/v1/server/access/lookup {login} resolves a GitHub login to its numeric id through GitHub's public users API; organisations and bots are refused (github_not_user), unknown names are github_user_not_found. POST /api/v1/server/access/add {id} admits the id, or restores a withdrawn one to its same account; POST /api/v1/server/access/remove {id} withdraws web access only. POST /api/v1/server/access/role {id, administrator} designates an admitted id as administrator (true) or revokes such a designation (false): the role is recorded by the numeric id, held at once by a bound id and otherwise from the sign-in that binds it, so a renamed or reused login never receives it; a role site.json gives is operator_owned here. A change is in effect only when the reply arrives; 503 outcome_uncertain means it may or may not have been committed, and nothing is retried. Refusals are fixed codes shared with root's admin access CLI: runtime_admission_disabled, runtime_admission_full, admission_open, operator_owned, binding_drift, github_user_not_found, github_not_user, github_lookup_unavailable, github_org_not_found, invalid_team, broker_unavailable, and not_admitted for a designation of an id that cannot sign in. Administrator, session and CSRF are required.

source.description: operator: site.json; site_admin: a runtime entry; team: only a listed team's member record names the id; none: only the gateway's deny or an administrator designation remains.

state.description: allowed: admitted, not yet signed in; joined: admitted with an account; withdrawn: web access removed, the account stays; removed: a never-used admission was deleted (change reply only); denied: an unconfirmed withdrawal or leftover deny with no admission row; unlisted: an administrator designation whose admission root has since removed; left: a team row whose latest sign-in found the person in no listed team, so that sign-in was refused and the account stays; unconfirmed: a team row whose latest sign-in GitHub could not answer for, refused without being called leaving. removed also answers a dismissed leaver.

actor.description: The administrator's GitHub id or root, as the gateway reported it; provenance, not proof.

last_seen.description: The newest use of any live session, accurate to a day: the gateway renews a session's idle deadline at most daily. Absent when no live session can tell, including one whose idle deadline has reached, or stalled within a day of, its absolute one and no longer moves.

denied.description: The gateway refuses this subject. True on a row that is not withdrawn means a withdrawal was not confirmed.

team_state.description: The latest sign-in's team answer, on any row that has one: member (admitted through a listed team), left or unconfirmed.

teams.description: The listed teams the person was last confirmed in; for left, the teams left.

team.description: A listed GitHub team. Its active members may sign in: membership is asked of GitHub with the person's own token at each sign-in, and leaving takes effect at the next one.

pinned.description: A member check has bound the slug to the team's numeric id, so a later team that takes the slug never inherits it. Nobody is admitted through the team before that.

actor.description: The administrator's GitHub id or root, as the gateway reported it; provenance, not proof.

unavailable_at.description: GitHub did not answer the membership question at the latest sign-in that asked it: the organisation may not have approved Open Habitat's OAuth app, or GitHub failed. Cleared by the next answer.

administrator_role.description: The id's administrator role. operator: site.json declares it, and only root changes it; site_admin: an administrator designated it here and may revoke it. pending: granted at the sign-in that binds the id; granted: held now (administrator is true).

actor.description: The designating administrator's GitHub id; provenance, not proof. Only a designation carries it.

site_key_copy.description: The site AI key copy the site gave this person, at the sign-in that created the account or later by an administrator, from the gateway's own record: it says what was given, not what the person's Pi holds now. Only administrators' reads and the person's own read carry it.

suffix.description: The given key's last four characters.

current.description: The copy is of the key the site stores now.

receipt.description: What the sign-in that created the person's account did with the site's own defaults, recorded then and never updated. It says a clone was handed to the person's daemon, not that it finished, and holds no fact from the person's home. Only administrators' reads carry it.

outcome.description: no_access, check_failed: the gateway's own check with the sign-in token; queued, already_present: the daemon's handoff reply; unknown: that reply was missing or ambiguous; preselected: readable, and the mode only offered it in the chooser.

ai_key.description: The site AI key: seeded, already_present (the person's own credential stayed), failed, unknown (no reply), or not_offered.

mode.description: any: the installation admits anyone and the list is read-only.

runtime_admission.description: Root's switch; while false, add (of a person or a team) is refused, no new team member is recorded, and remove still works.
